general_ui_ux_design_guidelines: Design around the user's next decision, not just displaying every metric. Utilize progressive disclosure: overview first, depth on demand. The dashboard must feel like an elite command center, prioritizing network health and SLA statuses.

headings.usage: Use for all page titles, KPI numbers, and major section headers.

body.usage: Use for standard text, UI elements, and form labels.

mono.usage: MANDATORY for all numerical data: Coordinates, Dates, IP Addresses, Bandwidth, SLA durations, and Invoice numbers.

hierarchy_rules: H1 (Page Title): text-4xl sm:text-5xl tracking-tighter font-black
H2 (Section Header): text-2xl sm:text-3xl tracking-tight font-bold

layouts.overall_architecture: Sidebar-based navigation (left) with a massive central data canvas. The sidebar must be collapsible to maximize horizontal space for data tables.
layouts.dashboard_grid: Mode B: High Density Grid. grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-4. gap-4. Hero KPI in the top-left (col-span-1). Main charts take col-span-2 or col-span-3. Use 'align-items: stretch'.
layouts.data_entry_form: Multi-step 'Wizard' or Vertical Tabs on the left with the active section's form on the right. Avoid one massive scrolling page. Break into: Customer, SPK, Timeline, SLA, Media, BoQ, Invoice.

spacing.containers: p-6 or p-8 for main layout areas.
spacing.cards: p-4 or p-5 to maintain density while giving breathing room.
spacing.tables: Dense padding (py-2 px-3) to allow maximum rows on screen.
spacing.forms: gap-6 between form sections, gap-2 between label and input.

component_styles.surfaces: GRID BORDERS style. Expose the skeleton. Dashboards should feel like a technical command center. Minimal border-radius (rounded-sm or rounded-none).
component_styles.cards: Flat solid surfaces (#121214). 1px subtle border (#27272A). NO heavy drop shadows. On hover, slight border color change.
component_styles.tables: Shadcn Table heavily customized for density. Sticky header. Zebra striping using very subtle background shifts (#0A0A0C to #121214).
component_styles.forms: Shadcn form primitives. Inputs must have solid backgrounds (not transparent) to prevent text muddying. Focus state: ring-1 ring-blue-500 border-blue-500.
component_styles.buttons: Sharp edges (rounded-sm). Primary buttons in Brand Blue. Destructive actions in Status Red. Ensure text has 4.5:1 contrast.

visual_enhancers.tracing_beam: Apply to the active SLA target or the most critical alert card in the dashboard.
visual_enhancers.status_indicators: Use pulsating dots (ping animation) next to 'In-Progress' or 'Breached' SLAs.
visual_enhancers.empty_states: Include ASCII art or simple Phosphor line icons with a helpful message. No dead ends.

icons.usage: Use 'Duotone' or 'Regular' weight. Phosphor fits the dense dashboard look perfectly.

login_background.description: Abstract blue data network nodes. Use as the background for the login page with a heavy dark overlay (bg-black/80).

empty_state_illustration.description: Server rack lights. Use for 'No Data' or 'System Health' empty states with a grayscale filter and low opacity.

charts.styling: Remove all chart grid lines except horizontal baseline. Use mono fonts for axis ticks. Use solid fills (no gradients on bar charts) for a sharp, authoritative look.

instructions_to_main_agent: You are building a telecom command center. Prioritize data density, clarity, and authority.
Implement the multi-step form for Work Order data entry using Shadcn Tabs or a custom vertical wizard.
Always use IBM Plex Mono for coordinates, dates, and metric values.
Ensure the sidebar can be toggled/collapsed to give tables maximum width.
Do not use generic centered layouts. Left-align dense data.
For the data table, implement sticky headers and horizontal scrolling for the massive number of columns.
CRITICAL: DO NOT use complete transparent background in header, overlays, any surface that has content under it. Example: Dropdown with transparent background
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: You tend to converge toward generic, 'on distribution' outputs. In frontend design, this creates what users call the 'AI slop' aesthetic. Avoid this: make creative, distinctive frontends that surprise and delight.
Dark colors look good when used independently without gradients. DO NOT use dark colors as gradients.
Don't make generic centered layouts, simplistic gradients, and uniform styling.
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy.
Use glass-morphism effects carefully; prefer solid surfaces for data-heavy sections.
You MUST NOT apply universal transition. Eg: transition: all. Always add transitions for specific interactive elements.
You MUST NOT center align the app container, ie do not add .App { text-align: center; }.
Always use modern button styles like pill-shaped, or sharp button with interaction animations & color relevant to the app style.
NEVER use AI assistant Emoji characters like 🤖🧠💭💡🔮🎯 for icons.
Every interaction needs micro-animations - hover states, transitions, and entrance animations.
Use 2-3x more spacing than feels comfortable. Cramped designs look cheap, except inside data tables.
Missing categories (especially sponsor logos) = main agent will use placeholder text which is FORBIDDEN.
Prioritize using pre-existing components from src/components/ui when applicable.
All interactive and key informational elements MUST include a data-testid attribute to facilitate robust automated testing.
